text: Executive Summary This report presents the results of an initial techno-economic analysis for Susteon's direct air capture (DAC) technology, "EcoFilter," under project DE-FE0032254, “Bench-Scale Development of Promoted High- Capacity Structured Sorbents”. The analysis demonstrates that the process is potentially a cost effective for carbon dioxide (CO ) removal from ambient air. The EcoFilter is a modular air contactor containing a 2 structured sorbent comprised of a polymer backbone, a proprietary amine, and a promoter, coated onto a pleated filter structure. As a result, this sorbent has low water adsorption, high oxidative stability, and high adsorption rate. This technology is an improvement over Susteon’s previous DAC technology for which a technoeconomic assessment was conducted under DE- FE0032243. To determine this technology’s technoeconomic viability, a facility with a nominal CO capture rate of 2 100,000 TPY at a capacity factor of 85% was studied. This facility is assumed to be at a generic greenfield site in the Midwestern U.S. and is removing CO from air at standard conditions. The removed CO is then 2 2 transported and stored in a deep saline formation for which the cost is estimated using the Department of Energy (DOE) Office of Fossil Energy and Carbon Management (FECM)/NETL CO Transport Cost Model 2 (CO Transport Cost Model) and the FECM/NETL CO Saline Storage Cost Model (CO Storage Cost 2 2 2 Model). The output from DE-FE0032254’s analysis was compared to that developed during DE- FE0032243 and is illustrated below. As summarized in Table 1, results of this assessment show the cost of CO capture is $241/tCO using the 2 2 EcoFilter technology. To determine key process and cost parameters, a sensitivity analysis was conducted on technical and financial variables. A summary of the parameters and sensitivity analysis are provided in Table 3 and Figure 1, respectively. A combination of key performance improvements, notably CO 2 adsorption rate, sorbent capacity, manufacturing, and risk-reduction methods, can result in a reduction in cost of CO capture from $241/tonne-CO to $165/metric tonne-CO .
